newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan jails businessman for spying for China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan jails businessman for spying for China.

text.p: A Taiwan court has sentenced a local businessman to one year in prison for spying for rival China, state-funded Central News Agency reported on Tuesday.
The agency, quoting the court's verdict, said Chang Ming-ho was given a light sentence because he had turned himself in and his actions did not constitute a major threat to national security.

Chang, who ran a wedding gown store in China's Fujian province, confessed he had collected information on the island's defence budgets, foreign affairs, economic developments and investments for China over the past two years, the agency said.
Court officials were not available for comments.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since they split after a civil war in 1949. Taiwan has banned all direct official contacts with communist China.
But indirect commerce has flourished since the late 1980s when political tensions started to thaw. Some 30,000 Taiwan firms have poured more than US$30 billion into China.
